newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end higher, profit-taking pares gains.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end higher, profit-taking pares gains.

text.p: Profit-taking in the afternoon sheered off some of Thursday's trading gains, but sentiment remained good, especially towards cheap large-cap stocks, brokers said.
News that Daewoo Electronics would buy French consumer electronics maker Thomson Multimedia led Daewoo Group shares to dominate trading, they added.
The index ended 4.56 points higer to a provisional close of 839.73. Decliners just edged out advancers, 462 to 453.
Daewoo confirmed that it would buy Thomson from the Lagardere Group.

Daewoo Electronics ended at its upper limit of 7,420 won, up 420. Daewoo Heavy Industries headed the most active trading list, gaining 300 won to 7,300. Daewoo Corp climbed 280 won to 7,880, while Daewoo Telecom rose 500 won to 10,600.
Trading volume on the bourse was active, with 54.46 million shares changing hands.
"Tomorrow we expect more fluctuation of the index because domestic institutions seem set on taking profits," said a Dongsuh Securities broker.
But other brokers said the bourse would be supported by hopes for an interest rate cut.
The scheduled October 21 start of an employee stock savings plan was also expected to provide the market with new funds, they said.
Ssangyong Motor declined 160 won to 9,000 on profit-taking. Rumours, denied by the company that it was the target of a takeover bid, had recently jacked up the share price.
LG Metals, which had risen on expectations of good earnings, also fell. It lost 900 won to 19,700.
Cheap large-cap Samsung Heavy rose 600 won to 11,100 in active trading.
